header_signature.note: The header row isn't fixed: in the real export it's row 2, below a header line carrying the document number and date. The number here is a fallback to tell whether the sheet has any goods, not something to match against: the actual row is found by the recognizer.
header_signature.columns_note: The management-software reader reads by position (EAN from row[1], price from row[7]) and ignores headers. Positions 2-11 are the same in the real export and in the test fixture; column 1 carries the row marker «C» and has no header.

header_signature.note: «Totale» stays out of required: the real price list writes TOTALE and the test fixture writes TOTALI, and it's the same schema. The required columns are the same ones the dedicated reader needs.
header_signature.columns_note: BETULLA's reader reads by position (price from row[5]), so this also states where each header must sit. Measured on the real price list of 11 August 2026. Without it, one extra column at the front read 12.00 euros instead of 3.98 with no warning.

order_write.note: Where the ordered quantity is written inside the BETULLA price list. BETULLA's reader is dedicated and has no field_mapping: without this declaration, column C was hardcoded in the launcher, and no learned supplier adapter could ever become writable. «FIRST» here means the document's first sheet: it's declared by the registry, i.e. by someone who actually looked at the price list.

header_signature.note: Fingerprint learned from the profile of «Listino3_34.xlsx» and confirmed by the user. The required columns are the ones the mapping actually uses: those the reader can't work without.
header_signature.columns_note: Where each header sat in the document this schema was learned from. A column that moves downgrades to SCHEMA_VARIATO: the mapping also gives columns by number and by letter, and those follow position, not name.

order_write.note: Sheet and rows come from the mapping above, the one confirmed by the user; the order column is declared by the registry, and the mapping must agree, otherwise the order would land in a cell nobody has verified. Reading resolves by name, but the column the order is written to (G) is positional: one extra column at the front would move it without changing any name, and the write step would put quantities in the wrong column of the price list sent back.

order_write.note: Sheet and rows come from the mapping above, the one confirmed by the user; the order column is declared by the registry, and the mapping must agree, otherwise the order would land in a cell nobody has verified. adapters.note: ⚠ CIPRESSO sends TWO price lists with different schemas, and this is the second one. It isn't «the same price list with a changing sheet name»: the header row also changes, and there's one extra column. Here: a single sheet titled «Listino al <date>», headers on row 1, and the ORDINE column already in place at G. In «cipresso_v1»: sheet «Listino», one row of formulas above, headers on row 2, no ORDINE column. The two tell themselves apart because «ordine» is among the required columns here: a document without that column never reaches this entry, and one that has it isn't read by the other. The one that picks is «registro.riconosci», which checks every candidate and takes the one the document actually reads with.

header_signature.note: «FIRST», not the sheet's name: that name carries the price list's date and changes every week; the document has a single sheet, and the actual reader («prepare_manifest_sources.selected_sheet») takes sheet number one on «FIRST». Declaring «Listino al 10-08-2026» would have made the adapter expire the following Monday. ⚠ «sheet_selector» isn't used: it has been written in this registry all along, and no line of code reads it.
header_signature.columns_note: Where each header sits. Measured on «3listino_Cipresso.xlsx» on 22 August 2026. A column that moves downgrades to SCHEMA_VARIATO, and that's intentional: the mapping gives the order column by letter, and that follows position, not name.

order_write.note: Sheet and rows come from the mapping above; the order column is declared by the registry and the mapping must agree. Here the ORDINE header genuinely exists, and it's read from the document before writing is enabled: that's the difference from «cipresso_v1», where there's nothing above column G.

column_shape_signature.note: The Larice price list has no header row at all, and its sheets are named «Canvass 28 06-10lug»: there's nothing to read by name. Columns are recognized from how they're populated.

commercial_conditions.note: Where LARICE writes its commercial conditions and how they're laid out. «blocchi» means a condition spans several rows: the header with the quantity to buy, then the eligible goods, then the free-goods row. The names under «fields» are the columns declared in «column_map»: the position is written in a single place, so when the user confirms a schema change the conditions follow the prices instead of lagging a week behind. Measured on the 33-34 07-21 Aug price list on 15 August 2026: 13 threshold headers and 13 free-goods rows, all in column G, all reassembled in full.

row_markers.note: The texts that appear in the discount column. These are the codes allowed: any other text raises a warning, because it means the supplier has introduced a convention nobody has read yet.

adapters.note: ⚠ LARICE sends TWO canvasses with different schemas, and this is the second one: the one that has arrived since 4 September 2026 («New Larice N°37(v.0)»), headed «Larice Ingrosso Srl». It isn't the «larice_v1» price list with one column shifted: that one has no header row at all, keeps the EAN in R and prices in O; this one has real headers on row 11, the EAN in B, the list price in I, and the net price — discount already applied — in K. The two don't get confused because their signatures rule each other out: «larice_v1» requires at least 18 columns and this sheet has 16, this one requires its own headers and the other has none. It's added rather than replacing the other because the supplier can revert to the previous format from one week to the next.

header_signature.note: «FIRST» because the sheet is called «Canvass» but the document has only one, and the name has already changed once («Canvass 28 06-10lug» on the old format). Above row 11 sits the block with the supplier's data, the customer's, and the four totals: that's ten rows, and if one day it becomes nine the document downgrades to SCHEMA_VARIATO and says so, instead of silently reading the columns off by one.
header_signature.columns_note: Measured on «New Larice N°37(v.0)» on 4 September 2026: 6,548 rows, 16 columns. Column F has no header — it carries the word PROMO on rows under promotion — and column A is empty: that's why neither appears here.

field_mapping.note: The price the comparison uses is NETTO (K), not LISTINO (I): the SCONTO column's percentage is already applied inside K by the supplier. Declaring «unit_price_pre_discount» would trigger the branch that recomputes the discount and apply it a second time.

row_markers.note: This canvass doesn't flag the free-goods row: column F says PROMO on all goods under promotion, free goods included. The promotion engine recognizes it from the text — «IN OMAGGIO 1CT ...» — and that's the only way there is. Measured on 4 September 2026: six free-goods rows out of 6,537, zero false positives, and five of the six repeat the EAN of an item already in the price list at full price (8019580330416 sits at 0.68 as goods and 0.65 as the free item). Without this row, the comparison picks the free item's price.

order_write.note: The order column is D, under the QTA header. «header_row» and «data_start_row» are what held true on 4 September 2026: the actual rule is «expected_header_search», which searches for QTA in today's document. In the measured file, that word appears exactly once, in column D. If it's missing, or appears twice, the stored numbers are kept and validation rejects the document.

commercial_conditions.note: The conditions are laid out as on the old canvass — the header with the quantity to buy, then the eligible goods, then the free-goods row — but here they all sit in the same column E, free-item name included: that's why «text» and «reward» declare the same field. Measured on 4 September 2026 on «New Larice N°37(v.0)»: six threshold headers and six free-goods rows, all reassembled in full.

adapters.note: The format is decided by the file's first bytes, not its extension: an .xls is read with app/xls_reader.py, an .xlsx with openpyxl. This price list's signature is its headers, not the file name: Noce sends documents named, for example, formattato_104233.xls.

header_signature.note: The header sits on row 5, and row 4 carries a note («offer prices are in bold») that isn't a header. «descrizioneofferta» is among the required columns because, ever since the mapping reads it, the reader needs it: without it, reading would stop halfway through the file instead of reporting that the document doesn't have the expected shape.
header_signature.columns_note: Measured on formattato_104233.xls on 13 August 2026 (column A has no header). Reading resolves by name, but the order column (I, «quantita») is written by position inside their .xls: one extra column at the front would shift everything without changing any name.

field_mapping.availability_note: The «descrizione_offerta» column (P) is where Noce writes its offer conditions. Without this mapping, the availability field stayed empty on every record, and the promotion detectors never saw a row from this price list. In the 6 August 2026 file, the column is empty on all 8,851 rows kept, so the mapping changes nothing today: it opens the channel for when the supplier starts filling it in.

commercial_rules.line_total_source: The price list's Importo column holds the formula =I*H*E, i.e. cartons ordered times price per piece times pieces per carton: the price list itself states that the price is per piece and the order is in cartons.

order_write.note: Noce gets back **their own** file, not a conversion: the copy is written in place inside the .xls, four bytes per cell. Sheet, rows and the EAN column name are the ones from the field_mapping above.

column_shape_signature.note: The offers sheet arrives with no header row at all: above the products there are blank rows and just the word ORDINE in column H. There's nothing to read by name, so columns are recognized from how they're populated. ⚠ «There are prices, pieces per carton and barcodes» identifies nothing: almost every price list has those. What identifies this sheet is three things together — columns A-F filled, G EMPTY, and a single cell in H reading ORDINE. Without the empty G, any price list with its header on row 3 would land here and become «OFFERTE» (measured on 21 August 2026 on two sheets built specifically for the test).
